name: References Secret
description: A workflow file names a secret that exists AND that this repository can read. Derived from the collected workflow body, so it is an assertion about the FILE, not about what a run actually consumed. ONE EDGE PER DEFINING SCOPE: a name held at both organisation and repository scope is two credentials and gets two edges, because resolving to a single one would require knowing which environment the job selects, and that is chosen at runtime. Reach is derived, not assumed: an organisation secret shared with `selected` repositories is resolved against that list (the App can read it), and a `private` one reaches only private and internal repositories. A named secret this repository cannot read gets NO edge and is recorded in `tags.secret_refs.unresolved`, because at runtime the step receives an empty string exactly as it would for a name that does not exist — a credential a workflow cannot read is not one it uses. A referenced name matching nothing at all lands there too; minting a secret node from a reference would assert a credential exists on the evidence that somebody typed its name. The tag also carries `scopes_read` (a name is only unresolved with respect to scopes the run enumerated IN FULL — a refused listing and one truncated at the page cap both disqualify a scope) and `reach_uncertain` (the secret exists, but its selected-repository list was refused or truncated, so reach is undecided rather than absent). Two forms are invisible here and must not be read as 'references nothing': `secrets: inherit` passes everything without naming it, and an expression-driven job-level `environment:` chooses its secret scope at runtime.
